tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py:269-273: asserts recall==1.0, false_accept==0.0, kappa==1.0, stability_min==1.0 — all guaranteed by the mock, independent of the T10 rubric
advisory.finding: test_t10_eval_calibration_exercises_all_cases_with_stable_metrics asserts perfect calibration metrics (recall==1.0, false_accept==0.0, kappa==1.0, stability_min==1.0) against a _perfect_solve mock that emits a finding iff case['expect']=='finding' — the exact rule calibrate_criterion uses. `_fired` only checks `bool(verdict.get('findings'))` and never reads the `criteria:['T10']` label, so the mock hard-codes the very verdicts the metrics are computed from. The assertion verifies the metric arithmetic against a tautological oracle and exercises none of the T10 overlay's transient-vs-durable classification (the behavior this diff introduces); it would still pass if the rubric change were wrong.
scenarios: A regression in the T10 rubric that mis-classifies a transient probe as durable (or vice versa) would not be caught by this test — the mock, not the rubric or any solver, produces the verdicts.
